title: Jonathan, Son of Saul
lead: Saul's eldest son and heir, a bold warrior who became David's closest friend. He made a covenant with David, protected him from his own father, and died beside Saul on Mount Gilboa; David later kept faith with his son Mephibosheth.

sections.b: Jonathan first appears leading a thousand men at Gibeah (1 Samuel 13:2–3). With only his armor-bearer he climbs the cliff at Michmash and starts a rout of the Philistines, then nearly dies under his father's rash oath (1 Samuel 14). When David kills Goliath, Jonathan's life is "tied up" with David's; he makes a covenant with him and gives him his robe and weapons (1 Samuel 18:1–4). He pleads for David, warns him with arrows, and renews the covenant for their descendants (1 Samuel 19–20), meeting him one last time at Horesh (1 Samuel 23:16–18). He dies with Saul at Gilboa (1 Samuel 31:2), and David's lament calls his love "wonderful" (2 Samuel 1:26). David keeps his oath by caring for Jonathan's lame son Mephibosheth (2 Samuel 9:1–13; 2 Samuel 21:7).
